title: Maximum Discount 50%: Microsoft Launches AI to Help You Work, Copilot Turns into a Super App

content_html:
Technology media The Information published a post on September 22, stating that Microsoft is preparing to push enterprise customers to adopt Copilot with a more aggressive pricing strategy, while also launching a "super AI application." In the current intense competition for AI assistants, Microsoft is adopting a dual approach of "reducing prices + upgrading," aiming to move Copilot from an office assistance tool to an automation platform that can directly handle tasks for enterprises.

Enterprise subscriptions up to 50% off, possibly launched in October

Regarding discounts, it is reported that Microsoft has informed its sales team that it will offer more significant discounts on Copilot AI subscriptions for enterprise customers, with a discount range of about 30% to 50%. These discounts are expected to be implemented as early as October: companies purchasing 1,000 or more licenses can get a 30% discount, while customers with purchases of 10,000 or more licenses may receive a maximum discount of 50%.

For Microsoft, this means trading profit for market penetration. Copilot was previously sold as an AI add-on to Microsoft 365 for enterprises, but its adoption and actual active usage have always been tested by both price and effectiveness. Encouraging large customers to purchase in bulk at the highest discount rate is clearly aimed at consolidating positions in the competition against other vendors' AI office solutions and reducing long-term customer acquisition costs.

From Office Assistant to Automation Platform, Copilot Becomes a Super Application

In terms of product form, Microsoft plans to upgrade Copilot and launch what it calls a "super AI application," integrating AI coding tools and intelligent agent skills similar to OpenClaw. In other words, Copilot will no longer just be a Q&A, summary, and content generation assistant embedded in Office.

In Microsoft's vision, this super application will cover basic assistance in office scenarios such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Teams, and further extend into an automation platform: it can call tools, perform multi-step tasks, assist software development, and allow AI to truly participate in existing end-to-end workflows within enterprises. From "helping you think and write" to "doing it for you," this positioning shift means Copilot will touch more complex business processes and place higher demands on model reliability, permission management, and data security.

Overall, the price reduction aims to lower the trial threshold and quickly increase the number of installations, while the positioning of the super application aims to enhance usage depth and stickiness—when users entrust more processes to Copilot, Microsoft's influence in the enterprise AI market will also grow accordingly.
